scores.evidence: Critical path: identity and secrets → registry → deployment model → pilot to prod with rollback.
scores.rationale: Phases run from contracts and substrate (runners, registry, identity, envs) up to pilots, templates, waves, and progressive delivery, with a stated critical path and a hard rule on dependencies.

scores.evidence: Phase 2: Walking skeleton with 2–3 pilot services... commit → build → unit tests → image → dev → staging → manual promotion to prod → tested rollback.
scores.rationale: A real prod skeleton exists, but it comes after Phase 0 discovery and Phase 1 foundations rather than being the first phase, though Phase 1 does end with a hello-world deploy to dev.

scores.evidence: Choose the tools: CI engine, artifact registry, CD approach (GitOps with Argo CD or Flux, or a push-based tool), secrets manager.
scores.rationale: Irreversible tool choices are listed, and assumptions are stated up front, but there are no defaults with flip conditions.

scores.evidence: Avoid the most critical service... move the remaining ~15 services, including the most critical ones, after safe rollout features are in place.
scores.rationale: Shared platform work precedes services and critical services are moved last, but within-phase ordering by blast radius is not explicit, and the critical-last choice runs opposite to widest-first.

scores.evidence: Add these after the basic path works, so gates don't hold up adoption
scores.rationale: Short-lived OIDC credentials and signing appear in Phase 1, but scanning, SBOM, and admission policy are deferred to Phase 5, and migration phases have no security content.

scores.evidence: Add basic deployment notifications and links to dashboards.
scores.rationale: Observability shows up in the contract (structured logs), Phase 2, Phase 7 (SLO analysis), and Phase 8, but there is no concrete treatment in Phase 1 or the migration waves, and it is only loosely described as a parallel hook.

scores.evidence: Environment setup: dev, staging and prod clusters or namespaces, defined in infrastructure-as-code.
scores.rationale: IaC, immutable registry, versioned templates, and SHA artifact IDs give reproducibility, but it is not treated explicitly in each phase.

scores.evidence: Hard rule: don't move critical services until rollback is tested and progressive delivery exists.
scores.rationale: Tested rollback in Phase 2, parallel old/new pipelines in Phase 4, and automatic rollback in Phase 7 give some resilience, but it is not present in every phase.
The plan never addresses whether an AI layer applies, so there is no explicit N/A declaration.

scores.evidence: Add these after the basic path works... Add self-service through a developer portal, cost visibility for runners, and preview environments.
scores.rationale: Later items are placed in later phases with some conditions (warn to blocking, critical services after progressive delivery), but there is no explicit not-yet-built list with pull-forward triggers.

note: The plan is well sequenced and has a practical pilot-to-template-to-waves structure, but it lacks explicit decision defaults and flip conditions, defers security, and does not address the AI layer or threaded observability.
